title: Daily Quiz: Chemistry Class 9 — Fundamentals of Chemistry
subject: Chemistry

questions.question: The branch of chemistry that deals with carbon compounds is called:
questions.explanation: Organic Chemistry is the study of carbon compounds (other than oxides, carbonates etc.).

questions.question: The chemical symbol for Sodium is:
questions.explanation: Na comes from the Latin name Natrium for sodium.

questions.question: The smallest particle of an element that can take part in a chemical reaction is:
questions.explanation: An atom is the smallest particle of an element that takes part in a chemical reaction.

questions.question: The molecular mass of water (H2O) is:
The empirical formula of glucose (C6H12O6) is:
questions.explanation: Dividing all subscripts by 6 gives the simplest ratio CH2O.

questions.question: Avogadro's number is equal to:
questions.explanation: One mole of any substance contains 6.022 x 10^23 particles.

questions.question: The mass of one mole of oxygen gas (O2) is:
questions.explanation: O2 has molar mass 2 x 16 = 32 g/mol.

questions.question: Which of the following is a mixture?
questions.explanation: Air is a homogeneous mixture of many gases (N2, O2, CO2 etc.).

questions.question: The chemical formula of common salt is:
questions.explanation: Common salt is sodium chloride, NaCl.

questions.question: The percentage by mass of oxygen in CO2 is approximately:
questions.explanation: Mass of O in CO2 = 32 out of 44, so 32/44 x 100 = 72.7%.

title: Daily Quiz: Biology Class 9 — Biodiversity
subject: Biology

questions.question: The branch of biology that deals with the study of plants is:
questions.explanation: Botany is the study of plants; zoology is the study of animals.

questions.question: Binomial nomenclature was introduced by:
questions.explanation: Swedish botanist Carolus Linnaeus introduced the two-name (binomial) system of naming organisms.

questions.question: The scientific name of human beings is:
questions.explanation: Modern humans are Homo sapiens (genus Homo, species sapiens).

questions.question: The basic structural and functional unit of life is the:
questions.explanation: The cell is the smallest unit that can perform all life processes.

questions.question: Biodiversity means:
questions.optionC: Variety of all forms of life on Earth
questions.optionD: Number of forests in a country
questions.explanation: Biodiversity is the variety of living organisms at genetic, species and ecosystem levels.

questions.question: In the five-kingdom system, bacteria are placed in the kingdom:
questions.explanation: Prokaryotic organisms like bacteria belong to kingdom Monera.

questions.question: A species is a group of organisms that can:
questions.explanation: By definition, members of a species interbreed in nature and produce fertile offspring.

questions.question: In binomial nomenclature, the first name (genus) always begins with a:
questions.explanation: The genus name is capitalized; the species name starts with a small letter.

questions.question: The national animal of Pakistan is:
questions.explanation: The Markhor (Capra falconeri) is the national animal of Pakistan.

questions.question: Viruses are not placed in any of the five kingdoms because they are:
questions.optionB: Non-cellular and show living traits only inside a host
questions.explanation: Viruses are acellular particles that reproduce only inside living host cells, so they sit between living and non-living.

title: Daily Quiz: Mathematics Class 9 — Matrices and Determinants
subject: Mathematics

questions.question: The order of a matrix having 2 rows and 3 columns is:
questions.explanation: Order is written as rows x columns, so 2 rows and 3 columns give order 2 x 3.

questions.question: A matrix with an equal number of rows and columns is called a:
questions.explanation: A square matrix has the same number of rows and columns.

questions.question: The additive identity of a matrix is the:
questions.explanation: Adding a zero matrix of the same order leaves any matrix unchanged.

questions.question: The determinant of the matrix [[1, 2], [3, 4]] is:
A square matrix is called singular if its determinant is:
questions.explanation: A matrix with |A| = 0 is singular and has no inverse.

questions.question: The additive inverse of a matrix A is obtained by:
questions.optionB: Changing the sign of every element
questions.explanation: -A is formed by multiplying every element of A by -1, so A + (-A) = 0.

questions.question: Two matrices are equal if they have the same order and:
questions.explanation: Equality of matrices requires equal order and equality of all corresponding elements.

questions.question: A matrix in which all elements except the principal diagonal are zero is called a:
questions.explanation: In a diagonal matrix, all off-diagonal elements are zero.

questions.question: The product AB of matrices A and B is possible only when:
questions.optionB: Columns of A = Rows of B
questions.optionC: Rows of A = Columns of B
questions.explanation: Matrix multiplication requires the number of columns of A to equal the number of rows of B.

questions.question: The transpose of a 2 x 3 matrix has order:
questions.explanation: Transposing interchanges rows and columns, so a 2 x 3 matrix becomes 3 x 2.

title: Daily Quiz: Computer Science Class 9 — Computer Systems
subject: Computer Science

questions.question: CPU stands for:
questions.explanation: CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the brain of the computer that executes instructions.

questions.question: One byte is equal to:
questions.explanation: 1 byte = 8 bits.

questions.question: Which of the following is an input device?
questions.explanation: A keyboard is used to input data into the computer; the others are output devices.

questions.question: Which memory loses its data when the computer is switched off?
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile memory; its contents are erased when power is removed.

questions.question: The binary equivalent of decimal 5 is:
Which of the following is system software?
questions.explanation: An operating system is system software that manages hardware and other programs.

questions.question: First-generation computers used:
questions.explanation: First-generation computers (1940s-50s) were built with vacuum tubes.

questions.question: The ALU of the CPU performs:
questions.explanation: ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) performs calculations and logical comparisons.

questions.question: Which storage device is an optical medium?
questions.explanation: CDs and DVDs store data optically and are read by laser.

questions.question: The physical parts of a computer that we can touch are called:
questions.explanation: All tangible components of a computer system are its hardware.

title: Daily Quiz: English Class 9 — Parts of Speech & Tenses
subject: English

questions.question: In the sentence 'Honesty is the best policy', the word 'Honesty' is a:
questions.explanation: Honesty names a quality, so it is an (abstract) noun.

questions.question: Which sentence is in the Present Continuous tense?
questions.explanation: Present Continuous uses is/am/are + verb-ing: 'She is reading a book.'

questions.question: The past tense of the verb 'go' is:
questions.explanation: 'Go' is an irregular verb: go - went - gone.

questions.question: In 'The fast car won the race', the adjective is:
questions.explanation: 'Fast' describes the noun 'car', so it is an adjective.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:
questions.explanation: With he/she/it we use 'does not' + base verb: 'He does not like tea.'

questions.question: The synonym of 'begin' is:
questions.explanation: 'Begin' and 'start' have the same meaning.

questions.question: The antonym of 'ancient' is:
questions.explanation: Ancient (very old) is the opposite of modern (new, of the present time).

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'The book is ___ the table.'
questions.explanation: For something resting on a surface we use the preposition 'on'.

questions.question: The passive voice of 'She writes a letter' is:
questions.optionA: A letter is written by her.
questions.optionB: A letter was written by her.
questions.optionC: A letter is being written by she.
questions.explanation: Present Simple passive: object + is + past participle + by + subject.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the correct article: '___ sun rises in the east.'
questions.explanation: Unique things (the sun, the moon) take the definite article 'the'.

title: Daily Quiz: Urdu Class 9 — Qawaid
subject: Urdu

questions.question: کسی شخص، جگہ یا چیز کے نام کو کیا کہتے ہیں؟
questions.explanation: کسی شخص، جگہ یا چیز کے نام کو اسم کہتے ہیں، جیسے علی، لاہور، کتاب۔

questions.explanation: 'نو دو گیارہ ہونا' کا مطلب ہے چپکے سے بھاگ جانا۔

questions.question: جملہ 'یہ اچھا لڑکا ہے' میں اسمِ صفت کون سا ہے؟
questions.explanation: 'اچھا' لڑکے کی خوبی بیان کر رہا ہے، اس لیے یہ اسمِ صفت ہے۔

title: Daily Quiz: Islamiat Class 9 — Aqaid o Ibadat
subject: Islamiat

questions.question: پہلی وحی کس غار میں نازل ہوئی؟
questions.explanation: پہلی وحی غارِ حرا میں نازل ہوئی جو مکہ مکرمہ کے قریب جبلِ نور میں واقع ہے۔

questions.question: پہلی وحی میں قرآن مجید کی کون سی سورت نازل ہوئی؟

questions.explanation: اسلام کے پانچ ارکان ہیں: شہادت، نماز، زکاۃ، روزہ اور حج۔

questions.question: توحید کا مطلب ہے:
questions.explanation: توحید کا لغوی و اصطلاحی مطلب اللہ تعالیٰ کو اس کی ذات و صفات میں ایک اور یکتا ماننا ہے۔

questions.question: وحی لانے والے سب سے بڑے فرشتے کا نام ہے:

questions.question: زبور کس پیغمبر پر نازل ہوئی؟

questions.question: چاندی کے نصابِ زکاۃ کی مقدار ہے:

questions.question: حج کس اسلامی مہینے میں ادا کیا جاتا ہے؟

title: Daily Quiz: Pakistan Studies Class 9 — Ideology of Pakistan
subject: Pakistan Studies

questions.question: The ideology of Pakistan is based on the:
questions.explanation: Pakistan was demanded on the basis of the Two-Nation Theory: Muslims and Hindus are two separate nations.

questions.question: The Two-Nation Theory was first clearly presented by:
questions.explanation: After the Urdu-Hindi controversy of 1867, Sir Syed Ahmad Khan concluded that Hindus and Muslims were two separate nations.

questions.question: The Urdu-Hindi controversy took place in the year:
questions.explanation: The Urdu-Hindi controversy of 1867 in Banaras changed Sir Syed's thinking about Hindu-Muslim unity.

questions.question: The All India Muslim League was founded in 1906 at:
questions.explanation: The Muslim League was founded on 30 December 1906 at Dhaka.

questions.question: The Pakistan Resolution was passed on:
questions.explanation: The Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution was adopted on 23 March 1940 at Minto Park, Lahore.

questions.question: The name 'Pakistan' was proposed by:
questions.explanation: Chaudhry Rahmat Ali proposed the name 'Pakistan' in his 1933 pamphlet 'Now or Never'.

questions.question: Pakistan came into being on:
questions.explanation: Pakistan emerged as an independent state on 14 August 1947 (27 Ramadan 1366 AH).

questions.question: The first Governor-General of Pakistan was:
questions.explanation: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah became the first Governor-General of Pakistan.

questions.question: The Objectives Resolution was passed in:
questions.explanation: The Objectives Resolution was passed by the Constituent Assembly on 12 March 1949.

questions.question: Allama Iqbal presented his famous Allahabad Address in:
questions.explanation: In his 1930 Allahabad Address, Allama Iqbal demanded a separate homeland for the Muslims of the subcontinent.

title: Daily Quiz: Chemistry Class 10 — Chemical Equilibrium
subject: Chemistry

questions.question: A reversible reaction is represented by the symbol:
questions.explanation: The double half-arrow ⇌ shows that a reaction proceeds in both directions.

questions.question: At dynamic equilibrium, the rates of the forward and reverse reactions are:
questions.explanation: At equilibrium both reactions continue at equal rates, so concentrations stay constant.

questions.question: The Law of Mass Action was given by:
questions.explanation: Norwegian chemists Guldberg and Waage proposed the Law of Mass Action in 1864.

questions.question: According to Le Chatelier's principle, when a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it:
questions.explanation: The system adjusts itself in the direction that reduces the effect of the disturbance.

questions.question: Increasing pressure on a gaseous equilibrium shifts it towards the side with:
questions.explanation: Higher pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules (smaller volume).

questions.question: A catalyst at equilibrium:
questions.optionC: Only speeds up reaching equilibrium, without shifting it
questions.optionD: Changes the value of Kc strongly
questions.explanation: A catalyst speeds up forward and reverse reactions equally, so the position of equilibrium is unchanged.

questions.question: Dynamic equilibrium can only be established in a:
questions.explanation: In an open system products escape, so a closed system is required for equilibrium.

questions.question: For the reaction N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3, the Kc expression is:
questions.explanation: Kc = [products]^coefficients / [reactants]^coefficients = [NH3]^2 / ([N2][H2]^3).

questions.question: If the forward reaction is exothermic, increasing the temperature will shift the equilibrium:
questions.explanation: Added heat is absorbed by the endothermic (reverse) direction, so equilibrium shifts towards reactants.

questions.question: A very large value of Kc indicates that at equilibrium:
questions.explanation: Large Kc means the equilibrium mixture contains mostly products.

title: Daily Quiz: Biology Class 10 — Gaseous Exchange
subject: Biology

questions.question: In fish, gaseous exchange takes place through the:
questions.explanation: Fish absorb dissolved oxygen from water through their feathery gills.

questions.question: In humans, the actual site of gaseous exchange in the lungs is the:
questions.explanation: Millions of tiny air sacs called alveoli provide the surface where O2 and CO2 are exchanged with blood capillaries.

questions.question: The voice box of humans is called the:
questions.explanation: The larynx (voice box) contains the vocal cords that produce sound.

questions.question: During inhalation, the diaphragm:
questions.explanation: Contraction flattens the diaphragm, enlarging the chest cavity so air rushes in.

questions.question: The percentage of oxygen in exhaled air is about:
questions.explanation: Inhaled air has ~21% O2; exhaled air still contains about 16% O2 (and ~4% CO2).

questions.question: In leaves, gaseous exchange occurs through tiny pores called:
questions.explanation: Stomata, controlled by guard cells, allow CO2 in and O2 and water vapour out.

questions.question: The products of aerobic respiration are:
questions.explanation: Glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy (ATP) in aerobic respiration.

questions.question: The normal breathing rate of an adult human at rest is about:
questions.explanation: A resting adult breathes roughly 16-20 times per minute.

questions.question: The trachea is also commonly known as the:
questions.explanation: The trachea (windpipe) carries air from the larynx to the bronchi and is supported by C-shaped cartilage rings.

questions.question: Asthma is a respiratory disorder in which the following become narrow and inflamed:
questions.explanation: In asthma the airways (bronchi/bronchioles) swell and narrow, making breathing difficult.

title: Daily Quiz: Computer Science Class 10 — Programming Fundamentals in C
subject: Computer Science

questions.question: The C programming language was developed by:
questions.explanation: Dennis Ritchie developed C at Bell Laboratories in the early 1970s.

questions.question: The extension of a C source code file is:
questions.explanation: C program files are saved with the .c extension.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid keyword in C?
questions.explanation: 'int' is the C keyword used to declare integer variables.

questions.question: In C, the printf() function is used for:
questions.explanation: printf() prints formatted output on the screen; scanf() is used for input.

questions.question: The modulus operator in C, which gives the remainder of a division, is:
questions.explanation: The % operator returns the remainder, e.g. 10 % 3 = 1.

questions.question: Which loop checks its condition at the end of the loop body?
questions.explanation: A do-while loop executes the body at least once before testing the condition.

questions.question: A single-line comment in C begins with:
questions.explanation: // starts a single-line comment; /* ... */ is used for multi-line comments.

questions.question: Which data type is used to store decimal (fractional) numbers in C?
questions.explanation: float (and double) store real numbers with fractional parts.

questions.question: In C, array indexing starts from:
questions.explanation: The first element of a C array is at index 0.

questions.question: Every C program starts execution from the function named:
questions.explanation: main() is the entry point of every C program.

title: Daily Quiz: English Class 10 — Tenses & Voice
subject: English

questions.question: Which sentence is in the Past Perfect tense?
questions.optionB: She had finished her work before he arrived.
questions.explanation: Past Perfect uses 'had + past participle' for an action completed before another past action.

questions.question: The passive voice of 'They built a house' is:
questions.optionA: A house is built by them.
questions.optionB: A house was built by them.
questions.optionC: A house has being built by them.
questions.explanation: Past Simple passive: was/were + past participle — 'A house was built by them.'

questions.question: The active voice of 'The letter was posted by Ali' is:
questions.explanation: 'Was posted' is Past Simple passive, so the active form is 'Ali posted the letter.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:
questions.optionA: Neither of the boys were present.
questions.optionB: Neither of the boys was present.
questions.optionC: Neither of the boys are present yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular, so it takes the singular verb 'was'.

questions.question: The synonym of 'rapid' is:
questions.explanation: Rapid means happening quickly — fast.

questions.question: The antonym of 'scarce' is:
questions.explanation: Scarce (in short supply) is the opposite of abundant (plentiful).

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect speech of: He said, 'I am busy.'
questions.optionA: He said that he is busy.
questions.optionB: He said that he was busy.
questions.optionC: He said that I am busy.
questions.explanation: In reported speech after a past reporting verb, 'am' changes to 'was' and 'I' to 'he'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'If it rains, we ___ at home.'
questions.explanation: First conditional: If + Present Simple, will + base verb — 'we will stay at home.'

questions.question: In the sentence 'He ran quickly', the adverb is:
questions.explanation: 'Quickly' describes how he ran, so it is an adverb of manner.

questions.question: The future indefinite tense of 'He plays cricket' is:
questions.explanation: Future Indefinite uses will/shall + base verb: 'He will play cricket.'

questions.explanation: دن کا متضاد رات ہے۔

questions.question: ضرب المثل 'اونچی دکان پھیکا پکوان' کا مطلب ہے:
questions.optionA: محنت کا پھل میٹھا ہوتا ہے
questions.explanation: یہ ضرب المثل اس موقع پر استعمال ہوتی ہے جہاں شان و شوکت زیادہ ہو مگر اصل معیار کم ہو۔

questions.question: 'دریا' کون سی جنس ہے؟

questions.question: لفظ 'نااہل' میں سابقہ کون سا ہے؟
questions.explanation: کسی لفظ کے شروع میں لگنے والا جز سابقہ کہلاتا ہے؛ 'نااہل' میں 'نا' سابقہ ہے۔

questions.question: لفظ 'قلم دان' میں لاحقہ کون سا ہے؟
questions.explanation: لفظ کے آخر میں لگنے والا جز لاحقہ کہلاتا ہے؛ 'قلم دان' میں 'دان' لاحقہ ہے۔

questions.question: غالب کا اصل نام کیا تھا؟
questions.explanation: مرزا غالب کا اصل نام مرزا اسد اللہ خان بیگ تھا اور 'اسد' پھر 'غالب' ان کا تخلص رہا۔

questions.question: رسمی خط کے آخر میں عموماً لکھا جاتا ہے:
questions.explanation: رسمی و دفتری خطوط کا اختتام 'والسلام' یا 'آپ کا مخلص' جیسے باوقار الفاظ سے کیا جاتا ہے۔

title: Daily Quiz: Pakistan Studies Class 10 — Constitutional Development
subject: Pakistan Studies

questions.question: The Lucknow Pact between Congress and Muslim League was signed in:
questions.explanation: The Lucknow Pact (1916) was the only agreement between Congress and the Muslim League; separate electorates were accepted.

questions.question: The Khilafat Movement was launched in:
questions.explanation: The Khilafat Movement began in 1919 to protect the Ottoman Caliphate after World War I.

questions.question: The Nehru Report was published in:
questions.explanation: The Nehru Report (1928) rejected separate electorates, disappointing the Muslims.

questions.question: Quaid-e-Azam presented his famous Fourteen Points in:
questions.explanation: The Fourteen Points (1929) were Jinnah's response to the Nehru Report, listing Muslim demands.

questions.question: The first Constitution of Pakistan was enforced in:
questions.explanation: Pakistan's first constitution came into force on 23 March 1956, making Pakistan a republic.

questions.question: The first President of Pakistan (under the 1956 Constitution) was:
questions.explanation: Major General Iskander Mirza became the first President of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan in 1956.

questions.question: The 'One Unit' scheme in West Pakistan was established in:
questions.explanation: One Unit was created in 1955 by merging all West Pakistan provinces into a single province.

questions.question: The 1962 Constitution of Pakistan was given by:
questions.explanation: Field Marshal Ayub Khan promulgated the presidential Constitution of 1962.

questions.question: The Tashkent Declaration between Pakistan and India was signed in:
questions.explanation: After the 1965 war, the Tashkent Declaration was signed on 10 January 1966.

questions.question: East Pakistan separated to become Bangladesh in:
questions.explanation: After the 1971 war, East Pakistan emerged as the independent state of Bangladesh in December 1971.

title: Daily Quiz: Chemistry 1st Year — Stoichiometry
subject: Chemistry

questions.question: Stoichiometry is the study of:
questions.optionB: Quantitative relationships between reactants and products
questions.explanation: Stoichiometry calculates amounts of reactants and products from balanced chemical equations.

questions.question: The molar mass of carbon dioxide (CO2) is:
The number of moles in 36 g of water (H2O, M = 18 g/mol) is:
questions.explanation: Moles = mass / molar mass = 36 / 18 = 2 mol.

questions.question: The limiting reactant in a chemical reaction is the one that:
questions.optionB: Is consumed first and limits the amount of product
questions.explanation: The limiting reactant runs out first and decides the maximum possible yield.

questions.question: The volume occupied by one mole of an ideal gas at STP is:
questions.explanation: At STP (273 K, 1 atm), one mole of any ideal gas occupies 22.4 dm3 (litres).

questions.question: The number of formula units in 0.5 mole of NaCl is:
The molecular formula of a compound tells us:
questions.optionA: Only the simplest ratio of atoms
questions.optionB: The actual number of atoms of each element in a molecule
questions.explanation: The molecular formula gives the exact count of each atom; the empirical formula gives only the simplest ratio.

questions.question: Percentage yield is calculated as:
questions.explanation: % yield = (actual yield / theoretical yield) x 100.

questions.question: The mass of 2 moles of sulphuric acid (H2SO4, M = 98 g/mol) is:
questions.explanation: Mass = moles x molar mass = 2 x 98 = 196 g.

questions.question: In the reaction CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O, the moles of O2 needed to burn 2 moles of CH4 are:
questions.explanation: The equation ratio CH4 : O2 is 1 : 2, so 2 mol CH4 needs 4 mol O2.

title: Daily Quiz: Biology 1st Year — Enzymes
subject: Biology

questions.question: Chemically, almost all enzymes are:
questions.explanation: Enzymes are globular proteins that catalyse biochemical reactions.

questions.question: The 'lock and key' model of enzyme action was proposed by:
questions.explanation: Emil Fischer (1894) suggested the rigid lock-and-key fit between enzyme and substrate.

questions.question: The 'induced fit' model was proposed by:
questions.explanation: Koshland (1959) proposed that the active site changes shape slightly to fit the substrate.

questions.question: The substrate binds to the enzyme at the:
questions.explanation: The active site is the specific region of the enzyme where the substrate binds and reacts.

questions.question: Most human enzymes work best at about:
questions.explanation: Human enzymes have an optimum temperature near normal body temperature, about 37°C.

questions.question: A competitive inhibitor reduces enzyme activity because it:
questions.optionB: Resembles the substrate and blocks the active site
questions.explanation: Competitive inhibitors have a shape similar to the substrate and compete for the active site.

questions.question: Which of the following can act as an inorganic cofactor for enzymes?
questions.optionB: Metal ions like Mg2+ and Zn2+
questions.explanation: Many enzymes need metal ions (cofactors) such as Mg2+, Zn2+ or Fe2+ for activity.

questions.question: The enzyme amylase digests:
questions.explanation: Amylase (in saliva and pancreatic juice) breaks starch into sugars.

questions.question: Enzyme activity is affected by:
questions.explanation: Temperature, pH, enzyme and substrate concentration all influence the rate of enzyme action.

questions.question: At very high temperature an enzyme stops working because it:
questions.explanation: High heat breaks the bonds maintaining the enzyme's shape, denaturing it and destroying the active site.

title: Daily Quiz: Mathematics 1st Year — Complex Numbers
subject: Mathematics

questions.question: The value of i^2 (where i = sqrt(-1)) is:
questions.explanation: By definition i^2 = -1.

questions.question: The conjugate of 3 + 4i is:
questions.explanation: The conjugate changes the sign of the imaginary part only: 3 - 4i.

questions.question: The modulus of 3 - 4i is:
The value of i^13 is:
The real part of (2 + 3i)(1 - i) is:
questions.explanation: (2 + 3i)(1 - i) = 2 - 2i + 3i - 3i^2 = 5 + i, so the real part is 5.

questions.question: The additive inverse of 2 - 5i is:
questions.explanation: Negating both parts: -(2 - 5i) = -2 + 5i.

questions.question: De Moivre's theorem is used to find:
questions.optionB: Powers and roots of complex numbers
questions.explanation: (cos θ + i sin θ)^n = cos nθ + i sin nθ gives powers (and roots) of complex numbers.

questions.question: On an Argand diagram, a complex number is represented as a:
questions.explanation: In the Argand plane, a + bi is plotted as the point (a, b).

questions.question: If |z| = 0 for z = a + bi, then:
questions.explanation: sqrt(a^2 + b^2) = 0 only when both a and b are zero.

questions.question: The value of i^100 is:

title: Daily Quiz: Computer Science 1st Year — Number Systems
subject: Computer Science

questions.question: The base of the hexadecimal number system is:
questions.explanation: Hexadecimal uses 16 symbols: 0-9 and A-F.

questions.question: The octal equivalent of binary 111 is:
questions.explanation: Binary 111 = 4 + 2 + 1 = 7 in decimal and octal.

questions.question: One kilobyte (KB) is equal to:
questions.explanation: In computing, 1 KB = 2^10 = 1024 bytes.

questions.question: The ASCII code of the capital letter 'A' is:
questions.explanation: Uppercase A has ASCII value 65 (lowercase a is 97).

questions.question: Decimal 15 is represented in hexadecimal as:
The output of a NOT gate for input 1 is:
questions.explanation: A NOT gate inverts its input: NOT 1 = 0.

questions.question: An AND gate gives output 1 only when:
questions.explanation: AND output is 1 only if all inputs are 1.

questions.question: BCD stands for:
questions.explanation: BCD (Binary Coded Decimal) represents each decimal digit in 4 bits.

questions.question: Two's complement representation is mainly used to store:
questions.explanation: Two's complement allows computers to represent and subtract negative integers easily.

questions.question: Which of the following is system software?
questions.explanation: An operating system is the core system software managing hardware resources.

title: Daily Quiz: English 1st Year — Grammar & Vocabulary
subject: English

questions.question: The synonym of 'transparent' is:
questions.explanation: Transparent means allowing light through — clear.

questions.question: The antonym of 'victory' is:
questions.explanation: Victory (winning) is the opposite of defeat (losing).

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:
questions.optionA: One of my friends are coming.
questions.optionB: One of my friends is coming.
questions.optionC: One of my friend is coming.
questions.optionD: One of my friends were coming yesterday now.
questions.explanation: 'One of...' takes a singular verb because the subject is 'one'.

questions.question: The idiom 'to break the ice' means:
questions.optionB: To start a conversation in a social setting
questions.explanation: 'Break the ice' means to ease initial awkwardness and start talking.

questions.question: One word substitution: 'A person who speaks many languages' is a:
questions.explanation: A polyglot knows or uses several languages.

questions.question: The passive voice of 'The teacher punished the boy' is:
questions.optionA: The boy is punished by the teacher.
questions.optionB: The boy was punished by the teacher.
questions.optionD: The boy has punish by the teacher.
questions.explanation: Past Simple passive: was + past participle — 'The boy was punished by the teacher.'

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect speech of: Ali said, 'I will go.'
questions.optionA: Ali said that he will go.
questions.optionB: Ali said that he would go.
questions.optionC: Ali said that I will go.
questions.optionD: Ali says that he would went.
questions.explanation: In reported speech 'will' changes to 'would' after a past reporting verb.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'He is fond ___ music.'
questions.explanation: The adjective 'fond' is followed by the preposition 'of'.

questions.question: The plural of 'criterion' is:
questions.explanation: 'Criterion' is a Greek-origin word whose plural is 'criteria'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:
questions.optionD: She is good with Mathematics subject the.
questions.explanation: We say 'good at' a subject or skill.

title: Daily Quiz: Urdu 1st Year — Adab o Qawaid
subject: Urdu

questions.question: 'بابائے اردو' کس شخصیت کو کہا جاتا ہے؟
questions.explanation: اردو زبان و ادب کی خدمات کی بنا پر مولوی عبد الحق کو 'بابائے اردو' کہا جاتا ہے۔

questions.question: مرزا غالب کا اصل نام کیا تھا؟
questions.explanation: غالب کا اصل نام مرزا اسد اللہ خان بیگ تھا؛ 'اسد' اور بعد میں 'غالب' ان کے تخلص رہے۔

questions.question: علامہ اقبال کا پہلا اردو شعری مجموعہ کون سا ہے؟
questions.explanation: 'بانگِ درا' 1924ء میں شائع ہونے والا اقبال کا پہلا اردو مجموعہ کلام ہے۔

questions.question: ایک چیز کو کسی دوسری چیز جیسی قرار دینا کیا کہلاتا ہے؟
questions.explanation: جب کسی چیز کو مشترک صفت کی بنا پر دوسری چیز جیسی کہا جائے تو اسے تشبیہ کہتے ہیں۔

questions.question: انیس و دبیر کس صنفِ سخن کے لیے سب سے زیادہ مشہور ہیں؟
questions.explanation: میر انیس اور مرزا دبیر اردو مرثیہ نگاری کے سب سے بڑے نام ہیں۔

questions.question: 'مقدمہ شعر و شاعری' کے مصنف کون ہیں؟
questions.explanation: مولانا الطاف حسین حالی نے 'مقدمہ شعر و شاعری' لکھ کر اردو تنقید کی بنیاد رکھی۔

questions.question: قصیدے میں شاعر عموماً کیا کرتا ہے؟
questions.explanation: قصیدہ کسی شخصیت کی مدح و ستائش میں کہی جانے والی نظم ہے۔

questions.question: مرثیہ زیادہ تر کس موضوع پر لکھا جاتا ہے؟
questions.optionB: واقعۂ کربلا اور شہداء کے غم پر
questions.explanation: مرثیہ حضرت امام حسینؓ اور شہدائے کربلا کے مصائب و فضائل بیان کرنے والی نظم ہے۔

questions.question: سرسید احمد خان کا مشہور رسالہ کون سا تھا؟
questions.explanation: سرسید نے 1870ء میں رسالہ 'تہذیب الاخلاق' جاری کیا جس سے اردو نثر و صحافت کو نئی روح ملی۔

questions.question: استعارے اور تشبیہ میں بنیادی فرق کیا ہے؟
questions.optionA: استعارے میں اداتِ تشبیہ اور وجہِ تشبیہ حذف ہوتی ہے
questions.optionB: استعارہ صرف نثر میں ہوتا ہے
questions.optionC: تشبیہ صرف عربی میں ہوتی ہے
questions.explanation: استعارے میں مشبہ یا مشبہ بہ میں سے ایک اور اداتِ تشبیہ حذف کر کے لفظ کو اس کے غیر حقیقی معنی میں استعمال کیا جاتا ہے۔

title: Daily Quiz: Chemistry 2nd Year — s and p Block Elements
subject: Chemistry
chapter: Chapter 2: s and p Block Elements

questions.question: The alkali metals belong to which group of the periodic table?
questions.explanation: Group 1 elements (Li, Na, K...) are the alkali metals of the s-block.

questions.question: The most electronegative element in the periodic table is:
questions.explanation: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity (about 4.0 on the Pauling scale).

questions.question: Which pair of elements shows a diagonal relationship?
questions.explanation: Lithium resembles magnesium because of their similar ionic sizes and charge density.

questions.question: Across a period from left to right, atomic radius generally:
questions.explanation: Increasing nuclear charge pulls electrons closer, shrinking the atomic radius across a period.

questions.question: Across a period, ionization energy generally:
questions.explanation: Smaller size and greater nuclear charge make electrons harder to remove across a period.

questions.question: The halogens are placed in group:
questions.explanation: F, Cl, Br and I are the halogens of Group 17 in the p-block.

questions.question: The noble (inert) gases belong to group:
questions.explanation: Group 18 contains the noble gases with completely filled outer shells.

questions.question: Which of the following oxides is amphoteric?
questions.explanation: Aluminium oxide reacts with both acids and bases, so it is amphoteric.

questions.question: Down a group, metallic character of elements:
questions.explanation: Atoms get larger down a group, lose electrons more easily, and become more metallic.

questions.question: Magnesium burns in air with a bright white flame forming mainly:
questions.explanation: 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO; magnesium oxide is the white ash formed (some Mg3N2 also forms).

title: Daily Quiz: Biology 2nd Year — Homeostasis
subject: Biology

questions.question: Homeostasis is the maintenance of a:
questions.explanation: Homeostasis keeps internal conditions (temperature, water, glucose etc.) stable despite external changes.

questions.question: The main excretory organ in human beings is the:
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter blood and remove nitrogenous wastes as urine.

questions.question: The structural and functional unit of the kidney is the:
questions.explanation: Each kidney contains about a million nephrons that filter blood and form urine.

questions.question: Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) mainly controls:
questions.optionB: Reabsorption of water in the collecting duct
questions.explanation: ADH (vasopressin) increases water reabsorption, producing concentrated urine when the body is short of water.

questions.question: Diabetes insipidus is caused by the deficiency of:
questions.explanation: Lack of ADH causes excretion of large volumes of dilute urine — diabetes insipidus.

questions.question: In mammals, toxic ammonia is converted into urea in the:
questions.explanation: The liver converts ammonia to less toxic urea through the ornithine (urea) cycle.

questions.question: The temperature-regulating centre of the human brain is located in the:
questions.explanation: The hypothalamus acts as the body's thermostat and triggers sweating or shivering.

questions.question: Sweating helps the body by:
questions.explanation: Evaporation of sweat from the skin surface removes heat and cools the body.

questions.question: Ultrafiltration of blood in the nephron takes place in the:
questions.explanation: High pressure in the glomerulus forces water and small molecules into Bowman's capsule.

questions.question: Birds and desert reptiles excrete nitrogenous waste mainly as:
questions.explanation: Uric acid needs very little water for excretion, an adaptation for water conservation and flight.

title: Daily Quiz: Mathematics 2nd Year — Differentiation
subject: Mathematics

questions.question: The derivative of x^5 with respect to x is:
questions.explanation: By the power rule d/dx (x^n) = n x^(n-1), so d/dx (x^5) = 5x^4.

questions.question: d/dx (sin x) equals:
questions.explanation: The derivative of sin x is cos x.

questions.question: d/dx (e^x) equals:
questions.explanation: e^x is its own derivative.

questions.question: The derivative of a constant (7) is:
questions.explanation: A constant does not change, so its rate of change (derivative) is zero.

questions.question: d/dx (ln x) equals:
questions.explanation: The derivative of the natural logarithm ln x is 1/x.

questions.question: To differentiate y = x^2 sin x, we use the:
questions.explanation: y is a product of two functions of x, so (uv)' = u v' + v u' (product rule) applies.

questions.question: d/dθ (tan θ) equals:
questions.explanation: The derivative of tan θ is sec^2 θ.

questions.question: The slope of the curve y = x^2 at x = 1 is:
questions.explanation: dy/dx = 2x; at x = 1 the slope is 2.

questions.question: If y = 3x^2 + 2x, then dy/dx at x = 1 is:
The chain rule is used to differentiate:
questions.optionB: Composite functions (a function of a function)
questions.explanation: For y = f(g(x)), dy/dx = f'(g(x)) x g'(x) — the chain rule.

title: Daily Quiz: Computer Science 2nd Year — Object-Oriented Programming in C++
subject: Computer Science

questions.question: Hiding the internal implementation details and showing only the necessary features is called:
questions.explanation: Abstraction shows essential features while hiding background implementation details.

questions.question: A class in C++ is best described as a:
questions.optionB: Blueprint or template for creating objects
questions.explanation: A class defines the data and functions; objects are its instances, just as a house is built from a blueprint.

questions.question: A constructor is a special member function that:
questions.optionB: Has the same name as the class and initializes objects
questions.optionD: Is written outside the class always
questions.explanation: Constructors have the same name as the class, no return type, and run automatically when an object is created.

questions.question: Inheritance in OOP mainly provides:
questions.explanation: A derived class reuses the properties and methods of its base class, avoiding rewriting code.

questions.question: The '::' operator in C++ is called the:
questions.explanation: '::' is the scope resolution operator, used to define member functions outside the class or access global scope.

questions.question: Function overloading is an example of:
questions.explanation: Overloaded functions are resolved by the compiler from argument lists — compile-time (static) polymorphism.

questions.question: A destructor in C++ is identified by the symbol:
questions.explanation: A destructor has the same name as the class prefixed with a tilde, e.g. ~Student().

questions.question: In C++, 'cout' is an object of which class?
questions.explanation: cout is a predefined object of the ostream class used with the insertion operator << for output.

questions.question: In C++, a class is defined using the keyword:
questions.explanation: The 'class' keyword declares a user-defined type grouping data and functions.

questions.question: Wrapping data and the functions that work on it into a single unit is called:
questions.explanation: Encapsulation binds data members and member functions together inside a class and protects data via access specifiers.

title: Daily Quiz: English 2nd Year — Grammar & Vocabulary
subject: English

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence:
questions.optionB: I have been waiting since morning.
questions.optionC: I has been waiting since morning.
questions.explanation: For an action continuing from a past point of time we use Present Perfect Continuous with since/for.

questions.question: The synonym of 'abandon' is:
questions.explanation: To abandon something means to give it up completely.

questions.question: The antonym of 'transparent' is:
questions.explanation: Transparent (see-through) is the opposite of opaque (not see-through).

questions.question: The idiom 'once in a blue moon' means:
questions.explanation: 'Once in a blue moon' describes something that happens extremely rarely.

questions.question: The passive voice of 'Someone stole my watch' is:
questions.optionA: My watch is stolen by someone.
questions.explanation: Past Simple passive with an unknown agent: 'My watch was stolen.' (agent usually omitted).

questions.question: Choose the correct indirect speech of: She said, 'I have seen the film.'
questions.optionA: She said that she has seen the film.
questions.optionB: She said that she had seen the film.
questions.optionC: She said that I have seen the film.
questions.optionD: She says she had saw the film.
questions.explanation: Present Perfect in direct speech changes to Past Perfect in reported speech: 'had seen'.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: 'He is senior ___ me.'
questions.explanation: Adjectives like senior, junior, superior and prefer take 'to', not 'than'.

questions.question: One word substitution: 'A place where birds are kept' is an:
questions.explanation: An aviary is a large enclosure for keeping birds (apiary is for bees).

questions.question: Choose the correctly spelt word:
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'occurrence' — double c and double r.

questions.question: The past participle of 'write' is:
questions.explanation: Write - wrote - written; the third form (past participle) is 'written'.

title: Daily Quiz: Urdu 2nd Year — Adab o Qawaid
subject: Urdu

questions.question: جدید اردو نثر کی بنیاد رکھنے میں سب سے اہم کردار کس تحریک کا ہے؟
questions.explanation: سرسید احمد خان کی علی گڑھ تحریک نے جدید اردو نثر، مضمون نویسی اور صحافت کی بنیاد رکھی۔

questions.question: 'شاہنامہ اسلام' کے مصنف کون ہیں؟
questions.explanation: حفیظ جالندھری نے اسلامی تاریخ پر مشہور طویل نظم 'شاہنامہ اسلام' لکھی؛ وہ قومی ترانے کے خالق بھی ہیں۔

questions.question: میر تقی میر کو کس لقب سے یاد کیا جاتا ہے؟
questions.explanation: میر تقی میر کو اردو غزل کی عظمت کی بنا پر 'خدائے سخن' کہا جاتا ہے۔

questions.question: مثنوی 'سحر البیان' کے شاعر کون ہیں؟
questions.explanation: میر حسن کی مثنوی 'سحر البیان' اردو کی مشہور ترین مثنویوں میں شمار ہوتی ہے۔

questions.question: 'آبِ حیات' کے مصنف کون ہیں؟
questions.explanation: محمد حسین آزاد کی 'آبِ حیات' اردو شعراء کے تذکرے اور تنقید کی بنیادی کتاب ہے۔

questions.question: حالی کی مشہور مسدس کا اصل نام کیا ہے؟
questions.explanation: 'مسدس حالی' کا اصل عنوان 'مدوجزر اسلام' ہے جو 1879ء میں شائع ہوئی۔

questions.question: ترقی پسند ادبی تحریک کا آغاز کس سن میں ہوا؟
questions.explanation: ترقی پسند مصنفین کی پہلی کانفرنس 1936ء میں لکھنؤ میں ہوئی جس سے تحریک کا باقاعدہ آغاز ہوا۔

questions.question: اردو افسانے کے بانیوں میں سب سے نمایاں نام کس کا ہے؟
questions.explanation: پریم چند کو اردو (اور ہندی) افسانے کا بانی اور سب سے بڑا افسانہ نگار مانا جاتا ہے۔

questions.question: غالب کے خطوط کی سب سے بڑی خصوصیت کیا ہے؟
questions.optionB: خط کتابت کو مکالمے اور ادبی رنگ دینا
questions.explanation: غالب نے اردو خطوط کو رسمی انداز سے نکال کر بے تکلف مکالماتی اور ادبی اسلوب دیا۔

questions.question: 'شاعرِ مشرق' کس کا لقب ہے؟
questions.explanation: علامہ محمد اقبال کو 'شاعرِ مشرق'، 'مفکرِ پاکستان' اور 'حکیم الامت' کے القاب سے یاد کیا جاتا ہے۔

title: Daily Quiz: Pakistan Studies Class 12 — Constitutional Development of Pakistan
subject: Pakistan Studies

questions.question: The present Constitution of Pakistan was adopted in:
questions.explanation: The unanimous Constitution of 1973 was adopted on 10 April 1973 and enforced on 14 August 1973.

questions.question: The first woman Prime Minister of Pakistan was:
questions.explanation: Benazir Bhutto became Prime Minister in 1988 — the first woman to lead a Muslim-majority country as PM.

questions.question: Pakistan became a member of the United Nations in:
questions.explanation: Pakistan joined the UN on 30 September 1947, weeks after independence.

questions.question: The Simla Agreement between Pakistan and India was signed in:
questions.explanation: The Simla Agreement was signed on 2 July 1972 after the 1971 war.

questions.question: The first Martial Law in Pakistan was imposed in:
questions.explanation: On 7 October 1958, President Iskander Mirza abrogated the constitution and imposed martial law; Ayub Khan soon took over.

questions.question: The Objectives Resolution became a substantive part of the Constitution as Article 2-A in:
questions.explanation: Through the Revival of Constitution Order 1985, the Objectives Resolution was inserted as Article 2-A.

questions.question: Under Article 251 of the 1973 Constitution, the national language of Pakistan is:
questions.explanation: Article 251 declares Urdu the national language of Pakistan.

questions.question: The term (duration) of the National Assembly of Pakistan is:
questions.explanation: The National Assembly is elected for a term of five years unless dissolved earlier.

questions.question: Geographically, Pakistan is located in the region of:
questions.explanation: Pakistan lies in South Asia, bordered by Iran, Afghanistan, China and India.

questions.question: The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) agreements were formally launched in:
questions.explanation: CPEC agreements worth billions of dollars were signed during the Chinese President's visit to Pakistan in April 2015.
